i.norm: Flattening a clustered POSIX token "-ZA" where only "Z" is a known option (and "A" is not), with stopAtNonOption enabled, should burst the token into the recognized option and then "eat the rest" of the input. The bursting produces: "-Z" -> the recognized option "--" -> the non-option marker inserted once a non-option char is reached "A" -> the unrecognized remainder of "-ZA" null -> the single trailing argument slot copied verbatim after "eat the rest" giving 4 flattened tokens in total.
Register a single option whose short name is "Z".
A mostly-empty argument array with the clustered token "-ZA" at index 5.
